memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Moses went up on the mountain, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered the mountain, and on the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from within the cloud." - Exodus 24:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses climbs the mountain, and the cloud of God's glory settles over it. Then something interesting happens: for six full days, nothing. Moses waits, enveloped in cloud, without a word from God. Only on the seventh day does the Lord call to him. Six days of silence before the voice came.

That waiting must have been difficult. Moses was close to God's glory yet hearing nothing, present but not yet spoken to. Many of us know that experience — a season where God seems near but silent, where we are waiting for direction that has not yet come. Moses' example teaches us to stay. He did not descend the mountain in frustration; he waited in the cloud until God spoke.

The cloud itself is significant. God's glory was truly present, yet veiled — near enough to see, hidden enough to protect. God often comes to us this way, genuinely present but not fully revealed, teaching us to trust rather than to demand clarity. If you are in a season of cloud and silence, do not mistake it for absence. God's glory may be settling over your situation even now. Wait with Him. His voice will come in His time, and the waiting itself is part of the meeting.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I in a season of waiting where God seems near but silent?
Can I stay in the "cloud" and trust rather than demanding immediate clarity?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when You seem near but silent, help me wait rather than run ahead. Teach me to trust Your presence in the cloud until You speak in Your perfect time. Amen.
